gap: No result ChatGPT got states that one pair, the Soundcore AeroFit 2 Pro ($179.99 at us.soundcore.com, sold out on 2026-11-17), switches between open-ear and in-ear ANC by moving its ear hooks. Expert Reviews found that its ANC 'fell some way short' and lost to the Shokz OpenFit Pro ($249.95), and the buds' rated battery drops from 7 h to 5 h with ANC on.
standout_why: There were no rival pages to compare against. ChatGPT ran no search and got no results for this chat, so its answer was a generic comparison table with no products, prices or reviewer names. Nothing it showed mentions a hybrid open/ANC pair, any price, or what you give up by trying to get both. Our current page doesn't mention the hybrid either. Its Bose link (bose.com/.../ULT-OPENEARBUDS.html) now returns HTTP 404.
decides: This confirms the shopper has to choose one style. The one product built to skip the choice has weak ANC according to a named reviewer, gets 5 h on the buds with ANC on, and is sold out at the maker. The page should say: open-ear (AeroFit 2 $129.99, C50i $69.99 at the low end) for all-day wear, running and calls; sealed ANC buds (Liberty 4 NC $99.99, Liberty 4 Pro $149.99) for commutes and planes. The hybrid gets a 'skip it' line with Expert Reviews' name on it. Bose Ultra Open is $199 at bose.com today, down from $349, which makes it $19 more than OpenFit 2 and $29 more than AeroClip 2.
